title: Make the test override helper all or nothing

blocks.text: The billing team's tests use a small helper, `Overrides.apply(target, values)`, to replace fields of the object under test before they run it. A flaky test led to a bad discovery: when one of the fields a test names can't be written, the helper fails half-way, after it has already replaced the fields before it, and the next test in the class runs against an object that is half overridden.
`apply` already looks the fields up, checks each one before writing any, and then writes them. Finish the `TODO` in `src/main/java/practice/Overrides.java`:

items: `writable(field)`: whether `Field.set` will write this field once it has been made accessible.

blocks.text: When you're done, a call that names a field `Field.set` would refuse fails before anything is written, and every field it would write is still accepted. About three lines in total.

cases.says: private instance fields and static fields that are not final are replaced
a static final field is refused up front, so the other fields of the same call keep their values
a record's field is refused up front with the helper's own exception
a final instance field of an ordinary class is replaced, not refused

origin.section: A Static Final Field and a Record Component Refuse the Write

concepts: Field.set refuses a static final field and a record's field with IllegalAccessException even after setAccessible(true), while an ordinary final instance field is written.
